headline_tag: Uptrend holds as banks open Bitcoin to everyday customers

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's call is to scale up the acquisition budget: the longer-term trend and the last three months both lean up, with high confidence (88/100 including today's news, 79 on market data alone), so this is a reasonable time to fund growth, weighted toward channels that bring active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price is sitting right on its 50-day average and the Fed decides on 27 October, grow the budget in steps and keep part of it flexible to pause if price closes below $81,564 (the 50-day average). This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a price call or trading advice.

reasons: Price is about 12% above its 200-day average and up 24% over 90 days.
About 70% of the last 90 days closed above the long-term average.
Price sits right at its 50-day average ($81,564), below the $86,603 30-day high.

watch: The longer picture leans up, but price is sitting almost exactly on its 50-day average ($81,564) while a fair number of people are betting on a rise with borrowed money. A close below $81,564 would test the uptrend; a move back above $86,603 would ease the worry.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger picture still leans up and news of banks opening Bitcoin to everyday customers adds a little support, but this week is a pause rather than a push. Short term, the mood leans mildly up: the Fear & Greed reading is a middle-of-the-road 55 out of 100, while a fair number of people are betting on a rise with borrowed money, which can make dips sharper. If price closes above $86,603 (the 30-day high) the short-term picture turns clearly up; below $72,649 (the 200-day average) it turns down, and in between expect choppy days. Calmer betting would firm this up and a sudden sharp drop would cool it, so steady, education-led campaigns fit this week.

Over the next month, the picture leans moderately up. Price is about 24% higher than three months ago and about 70% of the last 90 days finished above the long-term average, though the past week slipped about 2%. There is room to climb if price gets above $86,603 (the 90-day high); the move fades if price slips below $81,564 (the 50-day average), which is barely under today's $81,661. News is nudging this up a little, mainly BlackRock's filing for a Bitcoin fund with built-in loss protection (PANews); the Fed's 27 October decision is the next scheduled event, and holding above the 50-day line would keep growth campaigns well timed.

Over three to six months, the trend leans up with the most confidence of the three. Price is about 12% above its 200-day average, but that average is flat and price is still roughly a third below its record, so this is an early recovery, not a mature uptrend. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,649 (the 200-day average), with $66,935 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. News is adding a little here: Germany's savings banks began offering Bitcoin trading inside their banking apps on 19 October (PANews, citing dpa); a rising 200-day average would strengthen this read and supports steady investment in new-user acquisition.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into growth with a steady, confident tone: the bigger trend is up and banks are opening Bitcoin to everyday customers, but no rally is under way this week, so favour trust, access and education stories over urgency.

items.theme: Banks bringing crypto to everyday customers
items.why: Germany's savings banks started rolling out crypto trading in their mobile banking apps on 19 October, beginning with BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL and POL. JPMorgan put its dollar deposit token JPM Coin on Ethereum for institutional clients, and Deutsche Bank plans to launch crypto custody in Germany within weeks after EU approval. Prices of the coins involved barely moved today, so this is a slow adoption story rather than a price story.
items.marketing_angle: A strong trust and education topic: what it means that ordinary banks now offer Bitcoin, and how an exchange compares.

items.why: Visa and Mesh announced that users of partner wallets can spend crypto and stablecoin balances at about 175 million Visa merchant locations without a separate card. Mastercard launched a tool to screen stablecoin payments for fraud and sanctions risk, and Circle minted a combined 750 million USDC on Solana in two batches.
items.marketing_angle: Good content for new users: how spending crypto at a shop actually works and what stablecoins are for.
